subject: Production throughput drop + rising 500s — executive standby & customer comms
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production throughput drop + rising 500s — executive standby & customer comms

Team — TL;DR: TritonIQ (high-volume payments partner) is reporting a sustained throughput drop (~40% RPC completion) and elevated 5xx rate starting 08:45 PDT. Topline impact: customer latency 95p jumped from 120ms to ~1.6s, request errors at ~6% for a critical route. TritonIQ is on their morning spike and is starting to impact checkout flows.

Asking for immediate executive standby and two coordinated outputs:
- A public-facing status note for TritonIQ (we need a concise, empathetic status and ETA).
- A short internal war-room (15 min) to align on mitigations (fallbacks, scaled capacity, routing) and customer promises.

Initial asks:
1) Marissa — quick surface-level triage and current hypothesis (KV cache hot-shard? autoscaler lag?).
2) Rishi — if we need to bump Dedicated pool or enable emergency fallback policy, what's the estimated lead time?
3) Vivek/Laura — flag any sales/legal/comms implications (SLA/credits exposure).

I'm opening a bridge in 10 minutes on Zoom (link in Drive doc). Attaching incident-playbook-v2.pdf and a draft status note (customer-status-note-0900.md). Please keep responses short and action-oriented.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-playbook-v2.pdf (PDF)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throughput drop + rising 500s — executive standby & customer comms

Kim — quick triage: seeing a sharp increase in KV miss rates on the inference-cold-keyspace cluster starting 08:43 PDT. Two observations:
- The KV node serving that shard dropped underlying GPU process memory back to 80% used -> increased cache thrashing around 08:42.
- Autoscaler did not add nodes because the queueing signal (avg latency) is below our trigger threshold — CPU-based watch didn't capture tokenization backpressure.

Current hypothesis: prefix/KV cache evictions combined with an under-sensitive autoscaling rule are causing more model re-loads and higher tail latency -> 5xx in the frontend.
Immediate mitigations in parallel:
- Increase cache retention window on the affected shard (config change) — near-zero risk, low time to apply (~3–5 min).
- Temporarily raise autoscaler sensitivity for that pool to trigger +2 nodes (manual override) — needs infra approval; ~10–12 min.
- Route TritonIQ traffic to a compatible replica pool (same model family, slightly higher-latency SLO) while we stabilize — requires routing policy toggle (~4 min).

I'm on the bridge now. Uploading kv-cache-dump-20270608.log to Drive for post-incident analysis.

—Marissa
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime

Attachments: kv-cache-dump-20270608.log (log)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throughput drop + rising 500s — executive standby & customer comms

On bridge — agree with Marissa's hypothesis. Action items I'm kicking off now:
- Approve manual autoscaler override for pool inference-prod-us-west-2 (requesting +2 reserved nodes). ETA to up: ~9 minutes once infra confirms.
- Enable emergency routing policy: pin TritonIQ to fallback-replica-2 while we hold the cache changes. This will increase per-token cost ~10% but should reduce 5xx by removing hot-shard pressure.
- If traffic still degrades after +2 nodes and routing, we'll open a short maintenance window to restart the offending GPU process (estimated downtime per shard 30–60s).

Vivek/Laura — if we need to offer a one-off credit or SLA concession, we should position it now; finance needs a heads-up. I'm escalating to infra on the autoscaler override.

—Rishi
Director, Platform Reliability
From: Ben Carlisle <ben.carlisle@tritoniq.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@tritoniq.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:47:15 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased 500s during morning spike — urgent

Kim, this is urgent on our side. Our checkout success rate dropped to 92% between 08:45 - 09:10 which cost us several thousand dollars of processed payments failing and a material UX hit. We're receiving 500 errors with the body: "model-inference-timeout" and transaction-level timeouts from our side.

We need:
1) A clear ETA for a fix or a reliable rollback plan.
2) Whether a fallback to an older model or lower tokenization would be available to keep success rate high.
3) Confirmation you will send a proactive status update to our CS and exec teams (we have a call at 10:00).

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Ben Carlisle
Head of Integrations, TritonIQ
ben.carlisle@tritoniq.com
+1 415 555 0127

Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased 500s during morning spike — urgent

Ben — thank you for the note and for the sample request IDs. We're on this and have opened an executive standby to coordinate both technical mitigation and customer communications. Short answers up front:
- ETA: we expect visible improvement within 15–25 minutes as we apply the cache-retention change + autoscaler override; we'll confirm as events complete.
- Fallback: we can pin TritonIQ traffic to a compatible replica (older micro-optimized model variant) immediately; that will reduce feature latency pressure but may slightly change tokenization behavior for ~5 minutes during the transition.
- Customer update: yes — see proposed status below (please review):

PROPOSED CUSTOMER STATUS (send now + update at 10:00 call):
Hi Ben / TritonIQ team,

We’re actively investigating an increase in errors and elevated latency affecting a subset of requests for your production traffic this morning. Our engineers have identified cache pressure on a shard serving your requests and have implemented an emergency autoscaler override and a routing policy to a stable replica. We expect recovery to be visible within 15–25 minutes. We will provide another update at the top of your 10:00 PT call and follow up with a short incident summary and mitigation steps.

We recognize the impact on your checkout flow and are prioritizing stabilization and a post-incident remediation plan to prevent recurrence.

—Kim

Please confirm you want us to hit send on that note and if you want a more technical annex for your engineering team.

Attachments: customer-status-note-0900.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-stabilization note + next steps

Update from the bridge (status: *stabilized*):
- Timeline: cache retention change applied 09:31; autoscaler override +2 nodes completed 09:42; routing policy toggled at 09:46. Error rate fell from 6.1% to 0.8% over the next 14 minutes.
- Root cause (preliminary): hot KV shard evictions due to an under-tuned cache retention window combined with autoscaler sensitivity that relies too heavily on CPU signals.
- Immediate remediation: permanent change to retention window for that keyspace, adjust autoscaler to consider queueing latency signal, and expand our synthetic coverage for morning spike patterns.
- Customer communication: Kimberly sent the first status note at 10:05; Ben confirmed receipt and asked for a technical annex — we should prepare a short appendix with sample Request IDs and mitigation steps.

Deliverables / owners:
- Marissa: post-incident KV analysis and new retention default (ETA 48 hours).
- Rishi: autoscaler rule change + rollout (ETA 72 hours; will stage-canalize to avoid mass re-scaling).
- Laura/Vivek: commercial assessment for SLA exposure and credit calculation (ETA 24 hours).
- Kimberly: customer follow-up summary for TritonIQ execs and external postmortem (ETA 24 hours).

I'll upload a short incident log and the kv-cache dump to Drive (link above). Recommend we schedule a 30-minute readout tomorrow with product & infra to lock the remediation timeline.

—Marissa
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
